change_policy: Preserve this declaration and failed observations. Changes require a new profile identity, explicit rationale and new measurements; they cannot make this profile pass retroactively.

scope.topology: Permissioned HTTPS mesh; three independently configured owners, one service process and one restricted runtime DB role per owner; no mandatory manager.
scope.deployment: Linux server and native Windows/macOS Intel/macOS arm64 peer and SDK. Separate processes may share a test machine; this does not establish multi-organization or WAN availability.
scope.runtimes: All 12 native OS/CPU/CPython profiles in scripts/runtime-matrix.json, including actual child interpreters and installed packages.
scope.application: Explicit operator-selected installed factory; arbitrary registered callable, MAF workflow, MCP tool or A2A capability with application-supplied builder/checker/goal contracts. Received code is never imported.
scope.trust: Operator, installed application, DB administrator, filesystem and configured checkers are trusted within their declared scopes. Peer authentication does not establish business truth.
scope.paid_inference: Disabled in mandatory validation. An optional actual-model run needs explicit opt-in and a stated resource budget.
unsupported_claims: HA or multiple active writers for one owner
general collective intelligence or self-acceleration advantage

limits.retention: No automatic deletion of signed records, withdrawals, call maps, active evidence or unresolved leases. Report capacity and retention warnings; backup before operator-directed archival. Capacity refusal must preserve existing records.

required_services: one reviewed OSS TLS reverse proxy
required_injections: owner Python clock offset plus DB clock checks
fault_protocol.invariants: Every injection retains original IDs, uncertainty, mappings, budgets, signed history and finite operation bounds. Query/reconcile never invokes an uncertain effect again. Independent peer failures preserve valid sibling proposals.
fault_protocol.upgrade: Actual installed 0.3.2 -> drain -> coherent backup -> 0.4.0 migration -> byte/history/budget/map verification -> restore-state -> sync/reconcile -> explicit resume; also fresh install. Offline upgrade only.

release_soak.execution_environment: Linux native, >=2 logical CPU and >=4 GiB RAM; actual machine, versions and contention recorded. Other native profiles run the short production gate, not an inferred hour-long result.
release_soak.input_protocol: Seed 401; varying document lengths, Unicode/whitespace, registered composition parameters and verification capacity. This is a deterministic application fixture, not a universal task benchmark. Every offered operation is recorded, including refusal, timeout, UNKNOWN and interrupted work.

measurement.latency: Monotonic client wall time; nearest-rank p50/p95/p99 per operation and per outcome, plus all offered outcomes. Censored operations report lower bounds and count; no success-only SLO.
measurement.rss: OS process resident set for each owner and owned descendants; separate PostgreSQL/proxy RSS. Python allocations are not RSS. Record start, warmup, peak and end.
measurement.costs: Keep CPU seconds, inclusive wall seconds, OPA time, DB time, bytes, allowances, unavailable tokens and currency separate. Do not sum overlapping parent/child durations.
measurement.state: Sample physical tasks, tracked DB work, held/released allowance, orphan/expired invocations, unresolved effects, check backlog/count/age, source freshness, disk growth and drain status.

release_soak.interpretation: Bounds are acceptance targets for this declared fixture and hardware envelope. Planned fault windows and reasons are recorded before the run and reported separately; they are retained in the overall denominators. A failed bound requires a minimal fix and a complete new run, preserving the failure.

matched_experiment.independent_units: Five independently initialized matched pairs; tasks/peers within a pair are dependent and are not additional independent samples.
matched_experiment.initial_conditions: Same installed production APIs, deterministic no-charge application, initial tools, MAF workflows, builder/checker contracts, public inputs, owner allowances and task sequence. Separate DB, artifacts, evidence and cache per arm/run.
matched_experiment.baseline: Static arm may reuse its own cache, invoke existing tools and use a fixed rational documented selection policy. It receives the same initial skills and checks and is not deprived of reusable results.
matched_experiment.split: Training/calibration and held-out inputs use disjoint deterministic generators and identifiers fixed by seed. No evaluator-driven retuning during evaluation. Development fixtures are separate and limit external validity.
matched_experiment.primary_outcome: Fraction of all 24 held-out next-generation tasks meeting the same independently checked application contract within budget/deadline; absent, FAIL, UNKNOWN and censored tasks remain in denominator.
secondary_outcomes: checked reusable capability under declared scope
time to first independently accepted next-generation task
matched_experiment.analysis: Report each matched pair and paired differences plus descriptive intervals, complete raw data and protocol deviations. No task-level independence assumption, post-hoc seed exclusion or general causal/intelligence claim. Preserve existing negative pilots.
matched_experiment.release_gate: All ten isolated arms execute or report explicit bounded censored outcomes through the production public path; raw data and complete resource accounting are retained. A positive adaptive difference is not required.

distribution_gates.build: One fixed wheel/sdist pair; all native source and installed core/agents/model profiles, rebuilt sdist, cross-platform signatures/artifacts and mixed interpreters validate that same pair.
distribution_gates.installed_assets: Starter, deploy/TLS assets, config/schema/reference/help and README/quickstart commands execute outside checkout in fresh directories with normal install resolution.
distribution_gates.supply_chain: All actual OS/CPU/Python extra resolutions receive complete license, vulnerability and SBOM checks. Review proxy/binary/OS/package-manager/model terms separately.
distribution_gates.publication: Only existing workflow.yml / pypi OIDC; no protection bypass, tag movement or rebuild substitution. Verify actual no-cache PyPI files and installed production path, then publish immutable GitHub Release evidence and truthful main documentation.
